the technical factors that most influence the quality of diffusion images and tractography results are the acquisition sequence (especially the number and spacing of diffusion-weighted images), the gradient amplitude, the gradient slew rate (the time rate of change of the gradient), and the number of diffusion-weighted directions.
the technical factors that affect DTI image quality and quantitative accuracy are interdependent, so that optimization of one factor may require adjustment of another factor.

the best diffusion imaging is performed at high magnetic field strength (≥3 T), using a high-order (≥b = 1000 s/mm2) diffusion gradient encoding, with multichannel radiofrequency coils and a parallel imaging acceleration factor of 3 or higher, and with a short echo time (TE) and short repetition time (TR).
